response.rationale: R5 best integrates the raw composite: left colon/rectal-sparing distribution, biopsy showing subepithelial edema and hemorrhage with acute inflammation and no granulomas, and recent progesterone-only contraceptive as a temporal drug-related risk. R4 shares segmental left colitis and elevated calprotectin, but the biopsy lacks Crohn's-specific features and the 3-week course is less decisive than the ischemic pattern.

rejected.why: Negative stool cultures and C. difficile assays directly disfavor infectious colitis; only bloody diarrhea is nonspecific.
IBD is an umbrella category that does not specify the ischemic mechanism and is less complete than R5.
Normal rectal mucosa and segmental left colon involvement contradict the continuous rectal-to-proximal pattern of ulcerative colitis.
Microscopic colitis typically has normal endoscopy and watery diarrhea; here there is visible ulceration and bloody diarrhea.
CT explicitly shows no diverticulosis, and there is no supporting raw span for diverticulitis.
